correctness.rationale: At generic P, side projection and vertex supporting-normal foot criteria are paired incidence dot-product inequalities. Within hexagon no two failed incidences share a side or vertex; the 12 incidence signs reduce to two copies of six linear halfplanes. Exactly six triangular bad caps each area 1/6, only six adjacent cap intersections each area 1/18, no positive-area triple cap intersection; independently recomputed rational clipping of all six caps and all subsets. K=#failed caps has P(K=2)=1/3 and E[K]=1, so K=0,1,2 each 1/3. Therefore N=12−4K and (side,vertex)=(6−2K,6−2K), with variance 32/3. Exceptional incidence lines have zero area.
residual_risks: At a polygon vertex multiple supporting normals give one distinct foot: count conventions must not count line choices.

broader_coverage.reasoning: First moment and broad incidence framework do not determine exact three probabilities 1/3 or variance 32/3. Even knowing N takes values 4,8,12 and mean8 leaves one free distribution parameter.
